findings: Atmosphere cohesive: rain, wet floor reflections, cyan architecture, readable typography and strong central ring landmark. Weapon and robot geometry remain simple and repeated; restrained small-arena presentation rather than AAA finish.

Objective labels, distances and post-recovery text made mission direction understandable. Recovery supplied useful health/ammo and encouraged continued movement. Optic precision produced satisfying critical kills.
Receiver versus tall pylon distinction takes attention. West prompt is actionable but strict threshold created repeated near-receiver correction under fire.
Close cover and pylons caused multiple collision corrections. Through-wall objective labels guide bearing but do not explain doorway approach.

Enemy optics orange and red projectiles are visible, but crowded small threat badges and peripheral arrows were difficult to map quickly to actual shooters. Repeated side attacks punished stationary recovery and reload. Some shots wasted after enemies moved; synthetic tracking is a material confound.

Extraction requirement was clear and decay feedback immediate. Staying inside the small zone while dodging was difficult; short strafes left zone. I did not effectively exploit split blast baffles and died after three cores, so cannot establish whether final balance is fair for continuous human play.
ratingsRationale: Coherent playable short mission with clear objective loop and learnable critical combat, but navigation collisions, busy threat interpretation and final hold challenge reduced fluency in these two attempts. Presentation is polished for a compact prototype, without the asset variety, animation detail or breadth expected of AAA.
